deep_dive.title: The Other Half of the Memory Wall: Serving 35B MoEs from SSD with Trained Routing Prediction
deep_dive.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference on consumer hardware is bounded by weight memory: a 35B-class model is 19.5GB at 4-bit, and sparsity shrinks the compute per token, not the bytes that must be held. Naive offloading to SSD does not help on its own, because layer N+1's experts must be chosen before layer N's output exists, so the reads cannot start early enough to hide behind compute. We present Edge0, a streaming MoE inference engine that closes the gap with a prerouter: a per-layer head predicts the next layer's routing one token ahead, and the prediction is consumed as the routing itself, so the staged expert set equals the routed set and nothing is dropped. An unmerged recovery LoRA, trained on the student path, pays back the quality lost to int4 quantization and routing replacement. On a single 24GB machine, Edge0 serves a 35B MoE at 20tok/s inside 3GiB of peak active memory, within a few points of its fp16 teacher on average across five public benchmarks. An 8B tier runs on the same framework, and the framework, checkpoints, and adapters are open source.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: MoE inference is bounded by weight memory, so naive SSD offloading cannot hide reads since next-layer experts are chosen too late. Edge0 uses a per-layer prerouter to predict routing one token ahead, hiding SSD latency and serving 35B MoEs on consumer hardware.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 消费级硬件上运行MoE推理受限于权重内存，即便4位量化后仍需驻留大量字节，而朴素SSD卸载无法掩盖读取延迟，因为下一层专家必须在上一层输出前选定。本文提出Edge0流式推理引擎，利用逐层预路由头提前一个token预测下一层路由，并把预测直接作为路由使用，使预取的专家集与真实路由集完全一致。实验在35B级模型上验证了该方案能有效隐藏SSD读取开销，为大模型MoE在边缘设备上的部署提供了可行路径。
